THE STREAM, which is this entry's whole point: the picks come off `self.hooks.combat.combat_rng.card_selection`, the per-player CombatCardSelection stream that `Owner.Player.RunState.Rng.CombatCardSelection` names -- NOT the shared unseeded `combat._rng`. This is the seventh unit in this seam where that distinction was the trap, so the pin is written so it cannot silently regress: the test swaps an INDEPENDENT Random in for the accessor (in legacy mode the two are the same object, so a delegating spy would prove nothing) and asserts both that two picks came through it and that the shared rng's state is byte-identical afterwards. WHERE IT IS DISPATCHED, and why the record's 'genuine engine-shaped gap' framing was only half right. The pile is `PileType.Deck.GetPile(Owner.Player)` -- the RUN deck, not the combat's deep copy -- and a `CombatState` holds no run back-reference by design, so the combat-level `on_combat_end` genuinely cannot reach it. So no new engine capability was needed, only the rest of a walk that was already there -- the deep-copied deck was never the obstacle it was recorded as, because this effect never touches the combat's copy. `hooks=None` goes to CardCmd.upgrade deliberately: its outer `!IsEnding` is a COMBAT guard and this is a run-level effect running after the fight. EXECUTED 2026-07-29: Improvement 2 over a 4-Strike deck upgrades exactly 2; Improvement 3 over 3 cards upgrades all 3 once each; Improvement 5 over 2 upgradable cards upgrades 2 and does not raise; a deck of two Curses and a Strike upgrades only the Strike (Curses are not IsUpgradable, so the draw cannot land on one); it fires on a LOST combat too, which is what AfterCombatEnd-before-AfterCombatVictory means; and a bare CombatState that is never synced is inert. The sim's ImprovementPower declares only id, name and power_type. Its docstring (powers.py) states the reason -- 'the sim fights over a deep-copied deck and does not sync card upgrades back to the run, so the after-combat upgrade is a documented no-op here' -- and per binding rule 1 that is a DORMANT GAP, not a waiver: the divergence's shape is 'an effect the sim does not implement', and the dormancy rests on an engine property, not on scope. It is REACHABLE content: the applier is the ported Mad Science card's Improvement rider from the ported Act-3 Glory event Tinker Time, the same card that supplies power/curious. So a run can hold it, play it, and get nothing where the game permanently upgrades cards -- which is a run-level, conformance-visible difference (deck contents at the next floor). Two named triggers, and either is enough: wiring combat card upgrades back to the run deck, or a conformance replay that plays Mad Science with the Improvement rider. NOTE the sim also has no on_combat_end-time deck access to hang it on: hooks.py's on_combat_end is combat-scoped, so this is a genuine engine-shaped gap rather than a one-line omission -- which is why it is recorded here rather than fixed.
